# Sourcing Lab USA

> Sourcing Lab USA supplies custom packaging and textiles, sourced from factories. The contract and the invoice come from a company in France or China, named in your quotation.

This is an extended overview of the published business scope and a directory of source pages. It is not a copy of every page or article.

Contact: [contact@sourcinglabusa.com](mailto:contact@sourcinglabusa.com). [Request a quotation](https://sourcinglabusa.com/contact-us).

## The three pillars

### Product supply

Factory options, pricing, samples, and a written order for packaging and textiles.

Source: [Product supply](https://sourcinglabusa.com/china-to-us-procurement).

### Factory checks

Company records reviewed on every project. An on-site audit only if the quotation includes it.

Source: [Factory checks](https://sourcinglabusa.com/factory-verification).

### Cost before you order

HTS research and a landed-cost model. We do not book freight or clear customs.

Source: [Cost before you order](https://sourcinglabusa.com/landed-cost-analysis).

## What a supply includes.

### Included in a supply

- Product brief
- Factory search
- Pricing
- Samples
- Order and production follow-up

### Only if written into the quotation

- Third-party inspection
- Lab testing
- HS code classification
- Landed-cost model

### Outside our scope

- Customs clearance
- Freight forwarding
- U.S. storage
- A U.S. company formed for you

We are not a freight forwarder, a customs broker or an importer. Transport, insurance and U.S. entry are named in your quotation, or stay on your side.

Source: [Product supply and order terms](https://sourcinglabusa.com/china-to-us-procurement).

## Questions and answers

### What does Sourcing Lab USA do?

We supply custom packaging and textiles, sourced from factories. The contract and the invoice come from a company in France or China, named in your quotation. Clothing, sportswear and packaging are the business; other products are reviewed for feasibility on request.

### Who invoices my order, and who is the importer?

The company named in your quotation, in France or China, contracts with you and invoices the goods. Sourcing Lab USA is not the importer: the quotation names who handles transport, insurance and U.S. customs entry, or they stay on your side.

### What is included in a supply, and what is added only on request?

Included: the brief, the factory search, pricing, samples, the order and production follow-up. Only if written into the quotation: a third-party inspection, lab testing, HS code classification or a landed-cost model. Outside the scope: customs clearance, freight forwarding, U.S. storage and forming a U.S. company.

### How do you check a manufacturer?

Manufacturers are identified through our independent partnership in Shanghai and checked against your brief: the business registration and scope, whether the company makes the product rather than reselling it, and samples made to your specification. A third-party audit or inspection is added when it is written into the quotation.

### How do you limit quality fade between sample and production?

Quality fade can be reduced, not ruled out. The written specification and the approved sample are the reference for production. Payment milestones are set in the quotation; when a pre-shipment inspection is written into it, the final balance can be tied to its report.

### How do U.S. tariffs affect my order?

We look up the HTS code and estimate duties before you order. The customs entry is filed by the importer or the broker named in the quotation, not by us.

### What is the minimum order quantity?

As an indication, custom packaging and clothing commonly start around 500 units. The real minimum depends on the product, material, decoration and the split across sizes or colors, and it is confirmed in your quotation.

Source: [Homepage questions and answers](https://sourcinglabusa.com/#faq).

- [Product sourcing](https://sourcinglabusa.com/product-sourcing): Product brief, factory options, prices, samples and a written order.

- [Clothing and textiles](https://sourcinglabusa.com/custom-textile): Tech packs, materials, sizing, branding and sample approval.
- [Sportswear and technical apparel](https://sourcinglabusa.com/sportswear-sourcing): Fit, fabric and intended use; technical claims require evidence.
- [Private label packaging](https://sourcinglabusa.com/private-label-packaging): Structure, print and product information for a brand.
- [Private label manufacturing](https://sourcinglabusa.com/private-label-manufacturing): Product customization, samples and order terms.
- [Product development](https://sourcinglabusa.com/product-development): Specifications and samples before production.
- [China sourcing](https://sourcinglabusa.com/china-sourcing-agent): Factory search through the independent China partnership and product supply.
- [China-to-U.S. procurement](https://sourcinglabusa.com/china-to-us-procurement): Contracting company, invoicing and responsibilities agreed per order.

## Factory checks and cost before ordering

- [Factory verification](https://sourcinglabusa.com/factory-verification): Company records and supplier checks; on-site audits only when included in the quotation.
- [Quality control](https://sourcinglabusa.com/quality-control-china): Written specifications and approved samples; an inspection or lab test is coordinated only when quoted.
- [Landed-cost analysis](https://sourcinglabusa.com/landed-cost-analysis): A cost model only when included in the quotation, with transport and duty assumptions made explicit.
- [HS code research](https://sourcinglabusa.com/hs-code-consulting): Working classification research, subject to confirmation by the importer or customs broker.
- [HS code preparation tool](https://sourcinglabusa.com/tools/hs-code-finder): Prepare product information for classification review; the tool does not determine a code, duty rate or import requirement.
- [How we work](https://sourcinglabusa.com/how-we-work): The brief, factory search, quotation, samples, production follow-up and hand-off.

## Sourcing guides

- [FSC Certified Packaging Meaning: Sourcing from Asia](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/fsc-certification-explained): Understand what FSC certification means for packaging, how to verify suppliers in Asia, and the differences between FSC 100%, Mix, and Recycled.
- [Alibaba vs a Sourcing Company: Compare the Work and Order Terms](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/alibaba-vs-sourcing-company): Decide between direct supplier sourcing and a product supply partner with a task-ownership matrix, quote comparison and a practical packaging example.
- [Sourcing Furniture and Building Products from China: The Brief](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/building-materials-sourcing-brief): Prepare a U.S. project sourcing brief for furniture, cabinets, tiles and fixtures, with a specification register and specialist review checkpoints.
- [Canton Fair Sourcing Guide for U.S. Buyers: Brief to Follow-Up](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/canton-fair-sourcing-guide): Prepare a comparable RFQ, record supplier conversations and qualify candidates after the Canton Fair. Includes a downloadable meeting worksheet.
- [China Sourcing for U.S. Companies: A Decision-by-Decision Guide](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/china-sourcing-guide-us-businesses): Find manufacturers, qualify suppliers and compare quotes using a documented approval workflow, with RFQ, quality and landed-cost resources.
- [China Sourcing Quality Checklist: Samples to Shipment Decisions](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/quality-control-checklist): Create order-specific quality checkpoints for packaging and textiles, with a defect log, approval record and downloadable worksheet.
- [China Sourcing Agent Fees: Compare Scope Before Percentages](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/sourcing-agent-fees): Understand fixed fees, commissions and product supply pricing. Use a quote-completeness worksheet instead of assuming a universal sourcing fee.
- [How to Verify a Chinese Supplier: Evidence and Scorecard](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/verify-chinese-supplier): A supplier qualification matrix that separates identity, capability, samples and order terms. Download the evidence worksheet before approving an order.
- [China Sourcing RFQ Checklist: How to Prepare a Product Brief](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/china-sourcing-rfq-checklist): Prepare a China sourcing quotation request with product specs, quantities, samples and delivery requirements. Includes a free brief template.
- [Apparel Sourcing: Understanding Tech Packs and MOQ](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/apparel-sourcing-tech-packs-moq): Learn why a clear tech pack is essential for negotiating Minimum Order Quantities (MOQ) and defining product requirements when sourcing custom textiles.
- [U.S. Textile Import Planning: Labels, Documents and Product Review](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/importing-textiles-usa-checklist): Prepare a textile import review with product details, label artwork and documentation. Includes official FTC and CPSC resources for the U.S. market.
- [Sustainable Packaging Sourcing: Materials, Claims and a Better Brief](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/sustainable-packaging-ecommerce): Turn packaging sustainability goals into specific material and documentation requirements. Compare options for protection, structure and supported claims.
- [Custom Packaging MOQ: How to Plan a First Production Run](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/custom-packaging-moq-guide): Understand the factors that shape a custom packaging minimum order quantity and the information to confirm before you request a quote.
- [How to Discuss Material Claims When Sourcing Custom Textiles](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/sustainable-textile-sourcing): A practical way to define textile material requirements, request supporting documents, and avoid making claims that the order cannot substantiate.
- [How to Plan Landed Costs for Custom Packaging and Textile Orders](https://sourcinglabusa.com/blog/calculating-landed-costs-merchandise): A practical checklist of the cost items to confirm before ordering custom packaging or textiles from China to the United States.
